A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same VQ-Transplant study. The complete main text, Appendices A–D, 16 tables and nine figures are available and can be matched despite reformatting and changed pagination.

before.justification: V1 reports original image-reconstruction experiments across four datasets, synthetic non-Gaussian experiments, and comparisons of adaptation strategies and pretrained tokenizers.

after.justification: V2 retains these original empirical results in Section 5 and Appendices B–D, including reconstruction metrics, training-time comparisons and synthetic-data analyses.

M1.justification: The two-stage substitution/adaptation procedure, MMD-VQ objective and optional joint optimization in Appendix C are unchanged. Reordering the kernel/loss sentence in Section 4.2 does not change the method.

E1.justification: Both versions use ImageNet-1k, FFHQ, CelebA-HQ and LSUN-Churches for image reconstruction, together with the same synthetic mixtures spanning different degrees of non-Gaussianity.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain the same methods, including Vanilla, EMA, Online and Wasserstein quantizers and the published tokenizer baselines. Reordering Llama GEN and VAR in the baseline paragraph does not change participation.

E3.justification: Image processing, metrics, token counts, codebook sizes and training budgets remain unchanged. Appendix B also retains the same synthetic sampling design, dimensions and 10,000-step training procedure.

E4.justification: Both versions contain the same adaptation-duration and from-scratch comparisons, non-Gaussian sensitivity study, joint-versus-decoder-only analysis, LDM compatibility test and reconstruction examples.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. The tables and plots retain the same point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: Corresponding numerical entries and qualitative results match throughout the main text and appendices. For example, Table 2 retains r-FID 0.81 for MMD VAR with an 8192-entry codebook and 0.92 for the original VAR tokenizer.

T1.justification: The quantization objectives, MMD definition, Wasserstein expressions, Gaussian assumptions and synthetic-mixture definition are retained. Equations are renumbered and retypeset without substantive mathematical revisions.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion preserve the claims of efficient plug-and-play quantizer integration, MMD-based distributional alignment, near state-of-the-art reconstruction and a 95% training-cost reduction.

C2.justification: The decoder-mismatch explanation, Gaussian-feature interpretation, joint-optimization efficiency tradeoff and limitations of LDM adaptation remain unchanged in Section 5 and Appendices B–D.

D1.justification: Appendix A retains the same preprocessing, hardware, optimizer, learning rates, batch sizes and loss weights. Section 7 makes the same resource-availability statements, and the website and code/model links are unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works and positioning relative to earlier tokenizers and Wasserstein VQ are unchanged. Author-year citations, expanded author names and bibliographic formatting do not introduce new related work.

P1.justification: V2 makes limited wording edits, including rearranging the kernel/loss sentence in Section 4.2, and reformats citations and appendix cross-references. The section sequence, narrative and appendix organization remain essentially unchanged.

P2.justification: V2 adopts the ICLR template throughout, changing margins, headers, typography, caption formatting and display sizes and placement. Tables 2–3 now share a page, Tables 7–10 are grouped together, and Figures 4–6 precede the conclusion. All existing displays are retained.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially reformats the presentation but retains the same methods, results, appendix analyses and reproducibility information. The small wording edits and template conversion do not materially change the paper's scientific support or overall explanatory quality.
